Find out more about the completed trial here and published results here.  ### Phase 1 trial The phase 1 clinical trial tested the safety of Lenzumestrocel by injecting one dose into 8 participants with MND. The study measured changes to the participants vital signs such as breathing ability, heart health and blood tests, showing the treatment was safe.  ## Latest News ### 2026 July-  South Korea's Ministry of Food and Drug Safety announced that Neuronata-R has retained conditional approval for ALS in South Korea. CorestemChemon, the company behind the treatment, have also announced that they are planning to submit an application to the Food and Drug Administration next year. They hope that this application will lead to the approval of Neuronata-R  in the USA. The press release can be found here. ### 2025 September – Research findings from the ALSummit phase 3 trial were announced at the PACTALS congress. The trial failed to meet both primary and secondary endpoints to show a clear benefit in reducing MND progression across all participants. However, after 12 months, participants with a slower progression of MND showed a smaller decline in ALSFRS-R score, respiratory function and combined assessment of function and survival from the placebo control group. This data suggests the treatment may be beneficial for people with slow progressing MND. The company are in contact with the FDA following the subgroup findings and plan to submit a licencing application to make the treatment available for accelerated access in the USA. The press release can be read in full here.
